t1-grade-average.title: T1 Fix weighted grade average (1 file bug-fix)
t1-grade-average.prompt:
A student reported that `final_grade()` in the `gradebook` package returns wrong results
when the coursework weights do not add up to exactly 1.0, and that it crashes for a
student with no graded items.

Please fix the bug(s) in `gradebook/grades.py` so that:
- the final grade is the weighted average of the item scores, normalised by the sum of
  the weights that were actually used;
- items with a score of `None` (not yet graded) are ignored entirely;
- a student with no graded items gets `None` instead of an exception.

Run the existing test-suite with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` and make
sure it passes. Do not change the tests.

t2-duration-parser.title: T2 Implement duration parser + tests (feature from spec)
t2-duration-parser.prompt:
Implement `parse_duration()` in `timeutil/duration.py`. It is currently a stub.
The exact specification is in the function's docstring; `format_duration()` in the
same file already works and is the inverse operation for canonical strings.

Also add unit tests for `parse_duration()` to `tests/test_duration.py` covering the
valid and invalid cases from the specification.

Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` and make sure everything passes.

t3-schedule-conflicts.title: T3 Fix timetable clash detection (multi-file debugging)
t3-schedule-conflicts.prompt:
Bug report from the teaching office about the `scheduler` package:

> The weekly timetable checker reports far too many conflicts. Sessions that are
> back-to-back (one ends at 10:00, the next starts at 10:00) are flagged as clashing,
> sessions on different days are flagged as clashing, and every clash appears twice
> in the report.

`find_conflicts()` should return each conflicting pair exactly once, as a tuple
`(first, second)` ordered by the sessions' position in the input list, and the overall
list should be ordered the same way. Two sessions conflict when they are on the same
day, their time intervals genuinely overlap (touching end/start does not count), and
they share a room or a student group.

Investigate the package (the bug may involve more than one module), fix it, and run
`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` until it passes. Do not change the tests.
